prompt.adult: Martha welcomed Jesus into her house. Where did her sister Mary sit?
prompt.child: Jesus visited Martha's house. Where did Martha's sister Mary sit?
prompt.teen: When Jesus came to Martha's house, where did her sister Mary sit?
prompt.older: According to Luke 10:39, where did Mary sit when Jesus came to her sister's home?

verses.text: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard His word.

explanation.adult: Luke 10:39 tells where Mary sat and what she did there. Read the middle of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 10:39. It tells where Mary sat while she listened to Jesus.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 10:39. It says where Mary sat to hear Jesus.
explanation.older: Luke 10:39 states Mary's place while she heard His word.

teaching.extended_explanation: Luke 10:39 shows Mary sitting close to Jesus so she could hear His word.
teaching.takeaway: Mary sat at Jesus’ feet and listened to Him.

prompt.adult: While Jesus was visiting, what kept Martha distracted?
prompt.child: When Jesus was at her house, Martha was very busy. What was she busy with?
prompt.teen: What kept Martha distracted while Jesus was in her home?
prompt.older: According to Luke 10:40, with what was Martha distracted?

verses.text: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she approached Him and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Therefore tell her to help me.”

explanation.adult: Luke 10:40 tells what Martha was distracted with. Read the first part of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 10:40. The first sentence tells what kept Martha busy.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 10:40. The first sentence says what distracted her.
explanation.older: Luke 10:40 opens by naming what distracted Martha.

teaching.extended_explanation: Martha asked Jesus to send her sister to help. Luke 10:40 says what Martha was busy doing, and her words to Jesus say it too.
teaching.takeaway: Martha was distracted with much serving.

prompt.child: Zacchaeus was a rich man in Jericho. What was his job?
prompt.older: According to Luke 19:2, what was Zacchaeus's position?

verses.text: Now behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus who was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

explanation.adult: Luke 19:2 says who Zacchaeus was. Read the words after "who was a chief."
explanation.child: Read Luke 19:2. After his name, the verse tells his job.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 19:2. His job is named right after his name.
explanation.older: Luke 19:2 states his position immediately after his name, along with the fact that he was rich.

teaching.extended_explanation: Luke 19:2 gives three facts: his name, his job (he was the head of others who did the same work), and that he was rich.
teaching.takeaway: Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector.

prompt.adult: Zacchaeus wanted to see who Jesus was, but he could not because of the crowd. Why else could he not see?
prompt.child: Zacchaeus wanted to see Jesus over the people, but he could not. Why?
prompt.teen: Zacchaeus tried to see who Jesus was and could not because of the crowd. Why was that?
prompt.older: According to Luke 19:3, why was Zacchaeus unable to see who Jesus was?

verses.text: And he sought to see who Jesus was, but could not because of the crowd, for he was of short stature.

explanation.adult: Luke 19:3 gives two reasons Zacchaeus could not see. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 19:3. The last words tell why he could not see.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 19:3. After it mentions the crowd, the last words give another reason.
explanation.older: Luke 19:3 closes with the reason he could not see over the crowd.

teaching.extended_explanation: The verse says he was "of short stature." That is an older way of saying he was not tall. Read the last words of Luke 19:3.
teaching.takeaway: Zacchaeus could not see Jesus because he was short.

explanation.older: Luke 19:4 names the tree directly after "climbed up into."

prompt.adult: When the disciples rebuked those bringing children to Jesus, how did Jesus feel?
prompt.child: The disciples tried to stop people from bringing children to Jesus. How did Jesus feel about that?
prompt.teen: The disciples tried to stop children from being brought to Jesus. How did He feel?
prompt.older: According to Mark 10:14, how did Jesus react when the disciples rebuked those who brought the children?

verses.text: But when Jesus saw it, He was greatly displeased and said to them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not forbid them; for of such is the kingdom of God.

explanation.adult: Mark 10:14 tells how Jesus felt when He saw what happened. Read the words after "He was greatly."
explanation.child: Read Mark 10:14. Find "He was greatly." The next word tells how Jesus felt.
explanation.teen: Check Mark 10:14. Jesus' feeling comes after "He was greatly."
explanation.older: Mark 10:14 records Jesus' reaction right after "He was greatly."

teaching.extended_explanation: The disciples were sending the children away. Mark 10:14 tells how Jesus felt about that, then what He told them to do.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus was greatly displeased when the disciples tried to keep the children away.
